title: Do We Need a Third Covid Shot?

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, the companies that make COVID-19 vaccines stand to earn enormous profits from booster shots.
sentences.zh: 今天，生产新冠疫苗的公司有望从加强针中获得巨额利润。

sentences.en: So how exactly will we know when or whether we actually need them?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们究竟该如何判断何时需要或是否真的需要接种加强针呢？

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Rebecca Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事丽贝卡·罗宾斯。

sentences.en: It's Monday, July 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月19日，星期一。

sentences.en: Rebecca, I want to talk about why it is that we're all suddenly talking about booster shots for the COVID-19 vaccine.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，我想谈谈为什么我们突然都在讨论新冠疫苗加强针的问题。

sentences.en: And I suspect that it's in part because of the Delta variant.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑这在一定程度上是因为德尔塔变异株。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That's definitely part of it.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是原因之一。

sentences.en: I think we're always going to be having a conversation right around now about whether booster shots would be needed,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在本来就会讨论是否需要加强针，

sentences.en: in large part just because enough time has passed since many people got their first shots.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为许多人接种第一针疫苗已经过去了一段时间。

sentences.en: For some people, that's been a few months, but for others, it's been six, seven months at this point.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说是几个月，但对另一些人来说，现在已经过去六七个月了。

sentences.en: And so I think there was always going to be a question about how long that protection will laSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，关于这种保护能持续多久，一直都会是个问题。

sentences.en: That said, I think Delta has accelerated these conversations and given them new urgency.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为德尔塔变异株加速了这些讨论，并赋予了它们新的紧迫性。

sentences.en: The Delta variant is now the most dominant strain in the United States.
sentences.zh: 德尔塔变异株现在是美国最主要的毒株。

sentences.en: New infections, hospitalizations, even deaths are increasing when many predicted they would be at all-time lows.
sentences.zh: 在许多人预测感染率将处于历史最低水平时，新的感染、住院甚至死亡病例却在增加。

sentences.en: You know, Delta has contributed to cases rising across the United States.
sentences.zh: 你知道，德尔塔导致了全美病例的上升。

sentences.en: We know from the evidence that Delta is more contagious.
sentences.zh: 我们从证据中得知，德尔塔的传染性更强。

sentences.en: And it's, I think, contributing to a sense of uncertainty and insecurity about how far we've gone in tamping down the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这加剧了人们对我们在遏制疫情方面取得的进展感到不确定和不安。

sentences.en: The fast-spreading Delta variant is raising new concerns and increasing that push to vaccinate.
sentences.zh: 快速传播的德尔塔变异株引发了新的担忧，并加大了疫苗接种的力度。

sentences.en: Might some of us need a booster for this Delta variant?
sentences.zh: 我们中有些人是否需要针对这种德尔塔变异株的加强针？

sentences.en: We've got plenty of questions about the Delta variant and vaccines.
sentences.zh: 关于德尔塔变异株和疫苗，我们有很多疑问。

sentences.en: So how good are the vaccines now and how long do we expect that to last?
sentences.zh: 那么现在的疫苗效果如何？我们预计这种保护能持续多久？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, these are great questions on everyone's minds, not just parents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些都是大家关心的问题，不仅仅是家长们。

sentences.en: And that has really risen in the minds of people that have been vaccinated so far.
sentences.zh: 这确实已经成为目前已接种疫苗人群心中的一个重要问题。

sentences.en: So the good news is that there's not reason right now to suspect that immunity is waning.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，目前没有理由怀疑免疫力正在减弱。

sentences.en: The evidence that we've seen so far strongly, strongly suggests that the vaccines remain effective against the virus and its variants, including Delta.
sentences.zh: 我们迄今为止看到的证据强烈表明，疫苗对病毒及其变异株（包括德尔塔）仍然有效。

sentences.en: The other piece of good news is that even if you do have a case of COVID after getting fully vaccinated, the chances are vanishingly low that you'll be hospitalized or die.
sentences.zh: 另一个好消息是，即使你在完全接种疫苗后感染了新冠，住院或死亡的几率也微乎其微。

sentences.en: That's all really encouraging right now.
sentences.zh: 目前这些都非常令人鼓舞。

sentences.en: But the question is how long this protection will laSt.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这种保护能持续多久。

sentences.en: And that's why we're having this debate about whether, and if so, when, we might ultimately need a booster.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们正在争论是否需要，以及如果需要，何时需要最终接种加强针。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when we talk about a booster, what exactly are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论加强针时，我们到底在谈论什么？

sentences.en: And how is it different than the original vaccine?
sentences.zh: 它与最初的疫苗有什么不同？

sentences.en: So a booster shot is a second, third dose of the vaccine that you received that is meant to strengthen the immune response.
sentences.zh: 加强针是你所接种疫苗的第二剂或第三剂，旨在增强免疫反应。

sentences.en: It's called a booster because it boosts the immune response.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫加强针，是因为它能增强免疫反应。

sentences.en: And you've probably received plenty of boosters before.
sentences.zh: 你以前可能接种过很多加强针。

sentences.en: For instance, you probably get a tetanus shot every 10 years.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可能每10年接种一次破伤风疫苗。

sentences.en: Or with the vaccines that are given in childhood, you've probably gotten boosters after a few months, sometimes up to a year.
sentences.zh: 或者对于儿童时期接种的疫苗，你可能在几个月后，有时甚至一年后，接种过加强针。

sentences.en: And so when we're talking about boosters for COVID, there are two different forms that that might take.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈论新冠加强针时，它可能有两种不同的形式。

sentences.en: One is just the original vaccine, another shot of the same substance that you've already gotten two doses of.
sentences.zh: 一种就是原始疫苗，即你已经接种过两剂的同种物质的另一针。

sentences.en: But then there's a different version, which is an altered version of the vaccine that's designed specifically to target one or more virus variants of concern.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一种版本，它是疫苗的改良版，专门针对一种或多种令人担忧的病毒变异株。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: For example, like Delta.
sentences.zh: 比如德尔塔。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So with that example, the vaccine would be specifically altered to target the Delta variant.
sentences.zh: 以那个例子来说，疫苗会被专门改良以针对德尔塔变异株。

sentences.en: And theoretically, if it turns out that the vaccines become less effective over time, that could raise the protection back up to the levels we saw before.
sentences.zh: 理论上，如果事实证明疫苗的效果随时间推移而下降，这可以将保护水平提高回我们之前看到的水平。

sentences.en: So previously, the vaccines were above 90% effective.
sentences.zh: 之前，疫苗的有效率在90%以上。

sentences.en: And if it turns out that over time, they dropped to a threshold of 70% effectiveness at a population level, a booster could help raise that effectiveness level back up to, say,
sentences.zh: 如果事实证明随着时间的推移，它们在人口层面的有效率下降到了70%的阈值，那么加强针可以帮助将有效率提高回，比如说，

sentences.en: So I guess the question on everyone's mind is, do we need a booster shot?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜大家都在想的问题是，我们需要加强针吗？

sentences.en: So how should we be thinking about that?
sentences.zh: 我们应该如何考虑这个问题？

sentences.en: What does that discussion look like right now?
sentences.zh: 目前的讨论情况如何？

sentences.en: So we don't know the answer yet as to whether and if so, when booster shots might be needed.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道是否需要以及何时需要加强针的答案。

sentences.en: Some researchers believe we might never need a booster, that the data indicate that the protection we got from vaccines could last for years and years.
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员认为我们可能永远不需要加强针，数据表明我们从疫苗中获得的保护可能持续多年。

sentences.en: But there's been an interesting divergence between the signaling from the federal government and from Pfizer.
sentences.zh: 但联邦政府和辉瑞公司发出的信号之间出现了有趣的分歧。

sentences.en: So this started on July 8th.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于7月8日。

sentences.en: Developing story tonight, Pfizer is asking the FDA for emergency approval for a third dose of its COVID vaccine.
sentences.zh: 今晚的突发新闻，辉瑞公司正在向FDA申请其新冠疫苗第三剂的紧急批准。

sentences.en: Pfizer put out a statement saying that it was planning to seek authorization to give a third dose of its original vaccine.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞发表声明称，计划寻求授权，提供第三剂原始疫苗。

sentences.en: Pfizer says a booster within a year could bump up immunity and better protect against the highly contagious Delta variant.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞表示，一年内接种加强针可以提高免疫力，并能更好地抵御高传染性的德尔塔变异株。

sentences.en: The company says its internal data shows antibody levels jumped five to tenfold after that booster.
sentences.zh: 该公司表示，其内部数据显示，接种加强针后抗体水平跃升了五到十倍。

sentences.en: And the argument that Pfizer was making was that its data indicated that a third dose would boost the immune response, which is not surprising, but a good sign.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞提出的论点是，其数据表明第三剂将增强免疫反应，这并不令人惊讶，但这是一个好迹象。

sentences.en: And that there also might be a need for a third dose based on data that it was seeing about how antibody levels were evolving among people who had received doses months prior.
sentences.zh: 而且根据其观察到的几个月前接种过疫苗的人群抗体水平演变的数据，可能也需要第三剂。

sentences.en: And what Pfizer is looking for there is signs that those antibody levels are waning.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞在寻找的是抗体水平正在减弱的迹象。

sentences.en: Which might be a sign that it's time for a booster.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个需要接种加强针的信号。

sentences.en: That's one sign.
sentences.zh: 这是一个迹象。

sentences.en: However, some scientists are skeptical of that approach as a way of deciding whether booster shots are necessary because antibody levels are just one part of the immune response.
sentences.zh: 然而，一些科学家对这种决定是否需要加强针的方法持怀疑态度，因为抗体水平只是免疫反应的一部分。

sentences.en: So just because antibody levels are waning doesn't necessarily mean you're not protected.
sentences.zh: 所以仅仅因为抗体水平在减弱，并不一定意味着你没有受到保护。

sentences.en: There are other ways that the immune system may protect you when you're confronted by the virus, even if your antibody levels have fallen.
sentences.zh: 即使你的抗体水平下降，当面对病毒时，免疫系统还有其他方式来保护你。

sentences.en: So given that skepticism, what is the government's response to this argument from Pfizer that it might be time for a third shot,
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于这种怀疑态度，政府对辉瑞关于可能需要第三针的论点有何回应，

sentences.en: a booster shot of its COVID-19 vaccine and to its application for a booster shot to be approved?
sentences.zh: 即其新冠疫苗的加强针，以及其申请批准加强针的请求？

sentences.en: So the same day that Pfizer put out that announcement, the federal government put out a very unusual statement.
sentences.zh: 就在辉瑞发布公告的同一天，联邦政府发表了一份非常不同寻常的声明。

sentences.en: Within hours, the CDC and FDA releasing a joint statement undercutting that announcement, saying Americans who have been fully vaccinated do not need a booster shot at this time.
sentences.zh: 几小时内，疾控中心（CDC）和食品药品监督管理局（FDA）发布了一份联合声明，削弱了该公告的影响，称目前完全接种疫苗的美国人不需要加强针。

sentences.en: It was a joint statement from the CDC and the FDA,
sentences.zh: 这是来自CDC和FDA的联合声明，

sentences.en: and they said that they had not yet made a decision and there was not yet enough data to know whether booster shots would be needed at all.
sentences.zh: 他们表示尚未做出决定，且目前还没有足够的数据来判断是否需要加强针。

sentences.en: The CDC is saying Pfizer got out ahead of itself.
sentences.zh: CDC表示辉瑞操之过急了。

sentences.en: CDC and FDA officials say they are taking a wait and see approach.
sentences.zh: CDC和FDA官员表示，他们正在采取观望态度。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that we're not very, very actively following and gathering all of this information to see if and when we might need it.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们没有非常、非常积极地跟踪和收集所有这些信息，以观察我们是否以及何时可能需要它。

sentences.en: They emphasize that they would need much more time to collect data and examine multiple sources of information about the strength of immunity of the vaccines.
sentences.zh: 他们强调，他们需要更多时间来收集数据，并审查关于疫苗免疫强度的多种信息来源。

sentences.en: And a key part of that is looking at the breakthrough infection rates of people who've been fully vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 其中的关键部分是观察完全接种疫苗人群的突破性感染率。

sentences.en: In other words, they want to understand how many people who have been fully vaccinated are nevertheless contracting COVID.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们想了解有多少完全接种疫苗的人仍然感染了新冠。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because if that number is increasing, that might be a strong sign that the vaccines are not working as well as they were originally.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这个数字在增加，那可能是一个强烈的信号，表明疫苗的效果不如最初那么好了。

sentences.en: So basically, the government is telling Pfizer, hold your horses.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，政府是在告诉辉瑞，别急。

sentences.en: We don't think there's enough evidence that a booster is needed.
sentences.zh: 我们认为没有足够的证据表明需要加强针。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And that is a really unusual thing for FDA and CDC to do.
sentences.zh: 这对FDA和CDC来说是非常不寻常的做法。

sentences.en: So normally, the regulators would not put out sort of a signal one way or another about how they're thinking about data that they've yet to review.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，监管机构不会对他们尚未审查的数据如何考虑发表任何信号。

sentences.en: This, I think, was an unusual sign from the FDA and CDC.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是来自FDA和CDC的一个不同寻常的信号。

sentences.en: And we're in unusual times.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于一个不寻常的时期。

sentences.en: And these vaccines have not followed the normal precedent of FDA medical product reviews.
sentences.zh: 这些疫苗并没有遵循FDA医疗产品审查的常规先例。

sentences.en: So that's not surprising.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But I think it would be much more typical for FDA to stay silent and ultimately issue a decision or a signal once they are further along in the review process or once they've made the decision.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，更典型的情况是FDA保持沉默，并在审查过程进一步推进或做出决定后，最终发布决定或信号。

sentences.en: So how do you explain the government's very strong and unusual response?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何解释政府这种非常强烈且不寻常的回应？

sentences.en: Well, I think there's a key part of this here, which is the huge concern about the large swath of the American population that remains hesitant about getting vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这里有一个关键部分，那就是对美国仍对接种疫苗持犹豫态度的庞大群体感到极度担忧。

sentences.en: I think the government scientists are very cognizant of the skepticism among many in the public about just taking one or two shots of vaccine.
sentences.zh: 我认为政府科学家非常清楚公众中许多人对于仅仅接种一两针疫苗的怀疑态度。

sentences.en: And the idea that perhaps, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且这种想法，你知道，

sentences.en: a drug company would be looking to make money off of a shot that we're getting once a year for who knows how long is not going to help with that hesitancy.
sentences.zh: 一家制药公司想要从我们每年接种一次、不知要持续多久的疫苗中赚钱，这对消除这种犹豫毫无帮助。

sentences.en: I think it also might suggest that if the vaccines don't even work as well as they've been billed,
sentences.zh: 我认为这也可能暗示，如果疫苗的效果甚至不如宣传的那样好，

sentences.en: then people might be hesitant to get a vaccine dose in the first place if they're not yet vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 那么如果人们还没有接种疫苗，他们可能一开始就会犹豫是否要接种。

sentences.en: So I think the FDA and the CDC are very sensitive to those concerns,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为FDA和CDC对这些担忧非常敏感，

sentences.en: and they really wanted to signal that they would be acting independently and not just doing what a drug company was telling them.
sentences.zh: 他们真的想发出信号，表明他们将独立行事，而不是仅仅听从制药公司的指挥。

sentences.en: So the government is intent on showing it's not going to take direction from vaccine makers, and it wants to wait for evidence that vaccines actually need a booSt.
sentences.zh: 所以政府决心表明它不会听从疫苗制造商的指示，并且希望等待疫苗确实需要加强针的证据。

sentences.en: But isn't there a risk that that would mean waiting until it's too late when, if vaccinated people, potentially start getting COVID?
sentences.zh: 但难道没有风险吗？这意味着要等到为时已晚，如果接种过疫苗的人开始感染新冠？

sentences.en: Yes, that is certainly a risk.
sentences.zh: 是的，这当然是一种风险。

sentences.en: And I think that speaks to the kind of fine line that regulators are walking here,
sentences.zh: 我认为这说明了监管机构在这里所走的微妙界限，

sentences.en: because they don't want to make the call too early and spend huge amounts of money and capital persuading people to get shots that they might ultimately not need.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不想过早做出决定，花费巨额资金和资本去说服人们接种他们最终可能并不需要的疫苗。

sentences.en: But at the same time, if you wait too long, you're going to have more people infected and in potentially rarer cases, more people hospitalized or dying.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，如果你等待太久，就会有更多人感染，在更罕见的情况下，更多人住院或死亡。

sentences.en: So it's a tough decision about when to make a call one way or another.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个艰难的决定，关于何时做出某种决定。

sentences.en: And I think that's why FDA and CDC put out that statement, trying to emphasize how independent and data-driven they would be in the process.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么FDA和CDC发表了那份声明，试图强调他们在过程中将是多么独立和以数据为导向。

sentences.en: They're looking towards those breakthrough infection rates in the population that has already been vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 他们正在关注已经接种疫苗人群中的突破性感染率。

sentences.en: But they're also looking to other sources of information, like laboratory studies, looking at the immune response and how it evolves over time.
sentences.zh: 但他们也在关注其他信息来源，比如实验室研究，观察免疫反应及其随时间的演变。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So for now, there's a very live and very fascinating debate playing out between drug makers like Pfizer, who say it's time for a booster shot,
sentences.zh: 所以目前，在像辉瑞这样的制药商（他们说现在是接种加强针的时候了）和监管机构（他们说在准备做出决定之前我们需要更多证据）之间，正在进行一场非常活跃且引人入胜的辩论。

sentences.en: and regulators who say we need more evidence before we will be ready to make that determination.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 随着这场科学辩论的展开，这还有另一个层面。

sentences.en: And as this scientific debate is playing out, there's a whole other dimension to this as well.
sentences.zh: 那就是道德层面。

sentences.en: And that's a moral one.
sentences.zh: 许多公共卫生专家表示，在世界上还有这么多人甚至连一针疫苗都没接种的时候，讨论接种加强针是不道德的。

sentences.en: Many public health experts are saying that it's immoral to be having a conversation about giving booster shots at a time when so many people around the world have yet to receive even a single shot.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 那么，丽贝卡，请解释一下你刚才提到的关于加强针的道德辩论，以及具体是谁参与了这场辩论。

sentences.en: So, Rebecca, explain this moral debate that you just touched on when it comes to boosters and who is engaged in this debate specifically.
sentences.zh: 这场辩论归结为这样一个事实：在世界许多地方，特别是非洲和亚洲最贫困的地区，

sentences.en: So this debate comes down to the fact that in many parts of the world, particularly the poorest parts of Africa and Asia,
sentences.zh: 有许多国家甚至还没有为老年人、甚至是一些医护人员接种疫苗。

sentences.en: there are many countries that have yet to vaccinate even the elderly, even some of their health care workers.
sentences.zh: 而且在任何特定时刻，全球生产的疫苗剂量都是有限的。

sentences.en: And there's a finite number of doses that are being produced around the world at any given moment.
sentences.zh: 许多疫苗制造商正在研究可能的加强针。

sentences.en: A number of vaccine manufacturers are looking into possible booster shots.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞并不是唯一一家。

sentences.en: Pfizer is not alone in this.
sentences.zh: 莫德纳、阿斯利康、强生，他们都在研究额外接种一针的可能性。

sentences.en: Moderna, AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson, they're all at least studying an extra shot.
sentences.zh: 因此人们担心，如果疫苗制造商开始优先向富裕国家运送加强针，

sentences.en: So there's a fear that if the vaccine manufacturers start prioritizing shipments of booster shots to wealthy countries,
sentences.zh: 那可能意味着贫穷国家在获得第一针疫苗的排队中会被进一步推后。

sentences.en: that could mean that poor countries are going to get pushed even further back in line to receive even their first shots.
sentences.zh: 早上好，下午好，晚上好。

sentences.en: Good morning, good afternoon and good evening.
sentences.zh: 这场辩论正在公共卫生的最高层进行。

sentences.en: This debate is playing out at the highest levels of public health.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于一场日益严重的双轨疫情之中，国家之间的贫富差距日益扩大。

sentences.en: We're in the midst of a growing two-track pandemic where the haves and have-nots between countries are increasingly divergent.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织（WHO）总干事最近出来说……

sentences.en: The director general of the WHO, that's the World Health Organization, recently came out and said that...
sentences.zh: 与其让莫德纳和辉瑞优先向疫苗覆盖率相对较高的国家供应加强针，

sentences.en: Instead of Moderna and Pfizer prioritizing the supply of vaccines as boosters to countries whose populations have relatively high coverage,
sentences.zh: 我们需要他们全力以赴，将供应渠道转向疫苗覆盖率非常低的COVAX计划以及中低收入国家。

sentences.en: we need them to go all out to channel supply to COVAX and low- and middle-income countries which have very low vaccine coverage.
sentences.zh: 疫苗制造商应优先向COVAX供应疫苗。

sentences.en: Vaccine manufacturers should be prioritizing supply to COVAX.
sentences.zh: 那是旨在为世界贫困人口接种疫苗的项目，因为有太多的国家迫切需要他们的第一剂疫苗。

sentences.en: That's the program aimed at vaccinating the world's poor, since so many countries are in desperate need of their first doses.
sentences.zh: 现在的首要任务必须是为那些尚未接种任何剂量和保护的人接种疫苗。

sentences.en: The priority now must be to vaccinate those who have received no doses and protection.
sentences.zh: 你认为这些公司是否会优先向富裕国家提供加强针，而不是向贫穷国家提供第一针？

sentences.en: And do we think those companies are likely to prioritize boosters to wealthy countries over first shots to poorer countries?
sentences.zh: 我们认为这些公司是否会优先向富裕国家提供加强针，而不是向贫穷国家提供第一针？

sentences.en: What do the economics of the vaccine tell us about that?
sentences.zh: 疫苗的经济学对此有何启示？

sentences.en: Well, we don't know how this will play out,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们尚不清楚事态会如何发展，

sentences.en: but we do know that it would be more profitable for companies to prioritize shipments to wealthy countries simply because of how they're pricing vaccine doses.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，由于疫苗剂量的定价方式，制药公司优先向富裕国家发货会更有利可图。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: So Pfizer is charging different countries different prices for the vaccines, depending on their ability to pay.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞公司根据不同国家的支付能力，对疫苗收取不同的价格。

sentences.en: The United States, for example, is paying $19.50 for each shot of the Pfizer vaccine.
sentences.zh: 例如，美国每剂辉瑞疫苗支付 19.50 美元。

sentences.en: But poorer countries are being charged discounted prices, in some cases paying just for the cost of the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 但较贫穷的国家则享受折扣价，在某些情况下，支付的费用仅相当于疫苗的成本。

sentences.en: So the African Union, for instance, was able to secure doses that African countries will be paying from the range of $3 to $10 for.
sentences.zh: 例如，非盟成功争取到的疫苗剂量，非洲国家每剂只需支付 3 到 10 美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So far, far less than the almost $20 that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这远低于美国支付的近 20 美元，

sentences.en: is paying per dose.
sentences.zh: 每剂的价格。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so the drug companies would stand to make more money if they prioritize shipments to wealthier countries.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果制药公司优先向富裕国家发货，他们将获得更多利润。

sentences.en: Whether they'll actually follow through on that at a time when there's immense pressure and concern around vaccinating poor parts of the world is a different question.
sentences.zh: 在世界贫困地区疫苗接种问题引发巨大压力和担忧的情况下，他们是否真的会这样做，则是另一个问题。

sentences.en: So they'll be balancing those two considerations,
sentences.zh: 所以他们会权衡这两个考量，

sentences.en: the desire to make money with the optical concerns and the ethical concerns of prioritizing wealthy countries at a time when people are dying in poorer parts of the world,
sentences.zh: 即赚钱的欲望，与在贫困地区人们不断死亡时优先考虑富裕国家所带来的舆论和道德压力，

sentences.en: especially as Delta becomes a more intensifying threat.
sentences.zh: 尤其是随着德尔塔变异株威胁的加剧。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: How reasonable is it, Rebecca, to fear that booster shots are eventually going to become a kind of never-ending source of profit for pharmaceutical companies?
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，担心加强针最终会成为制药公司永无止境的利润来源，这种担忧有多合理？

sentences.en: And as a result,
sentences.zh: 结果就是，

sentences.en: those companies will inevitably be tempted to focus on boosters and getting boosters to wealthy countries rather than getting doses to the people who so desperately need them in poorer countries.
sentences.zh: 这些公司不可避免地会倾向于专注于加强针，并优先向富裕国家提供加强针，而不是向贫困地区那些迫切需要疫苗的人提供剂量。

sentences.en: And isn't that potentially why a company like Pfizer might be getting ahead of the CDC and the FDA in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这难道不是像辉瑞这样的公司可能抢在美国疾控中心和食药监局之前，

sentences.en: in pushing to get approval for a booster shot?
sentences.zh: 推动加强针获批的潜在原因吗？

sentences.en: I think this is definitely a reasonable fear, especially in the short term and the medium term, that we might see boosters prioritized over shipments to poorer countries.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是一个合理的担忧，特别是在短期和中期内，我们可能会看到加强针的优先级高于向贫困国家的发货。

sentences.en: That said, I don't think we'll see the general public getting booster shots unless there's a scientific consensus that they are needed.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为除非科学界达成共识，认为确实需要加强针，否则我们不会看到普通大众去接种。

sentences.en: And so I think both of these things could end up being true at the same time, that there is an urgent public health need for booster shots, but at the same time,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这两件事最终可能同时成立：一方面，公共卫生确实迫切需要加强针；但与此同时，

sentences.en: Pfizer and the other vaccine manufacturers could and would be making an enormous amount of money.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞和其他疫苗制造商能够且将会赚取巨额利润。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, the Pfizer vaccine is positioned to become one of the best-selling pharmaceutical products of all time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，辉瑞疫苗有望成为有史以来最畅销的医药产品之一。

sentences.en: That could be just for a year's worth of revenue.
sentences.zh: 这可能仅仅是一年的收入。

sentences.en: But if we end up getting booster shots annually or at some regular interval, that would change the financial calculus and, again,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们最终需要每年或定期接种加强针，那将改变财务计算方式，而且再次强调，

sentences.en: make this one of the most profitable medicines or medical products of all time.
sentences.zh: 这将使其成为有史以来利润最高的药物或医疗产品之一。

sentences.en: So at this point, given that we don't know that we need a booster, potentially ever, and certainly not at this very moment,
sentences.zh: 所以目前来看，鉴于我们不知道是否需要加强针，甚至可能永远不需要，而且肯定不是在这一刻，

sentences.en: the argument that the WHO is making would seem to be very compelling.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织的论点似乎非常有说服力。

sentences.en: That giving a very profitable vaccine to those already immune is not fair.
sentences.zh: 即向已经免疫的人提供高利润疫苗是不公平的。

sentences.en: But let's just say, in theory, that someday the call is made that we do need boosters.
sentences.zh: 但假设在理论上，有一天我们确实需要加强针。

sentences.en: Would it then be fair to ask vaccinated people who are suddenly being told that they do need an extra dose to wait for everyone else in the world to get their first doses?
sentences.zh: 那么要求那些突然被告知需要额外剂量的已接种人群，去等待世界上其他人接种第一剂，这公平吗？

sentences.en: Because couldn't that mean waiting a very, very long time?
sentences.zh: 因为那是否意味着要等待非常非常长的时间？

sentences.en: So when I talk to researchers at the WHO and elsewhere, they're very much focused on the now and what information we have available at this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以当我与世卫组织及其他地方的研究人员交谈时，他们非常关注当下，以及我们此刻掌握的信息。

sentences.en: And their main focus is saving the most number of lives.
sentences.zh: 他们的主要重点是挽救尽可能多的生命。

sentences.en: And the way to save the most number of lives is to focus on the developing world.
sentences.zh: 而挽救最多生命的方法是关注发展中国家。

sentences.en: And that's because fully vaccinated Americans already have strong immunity.
sentences.zh: 这是因为完全接种疫苗的美国人已经拥有了强大的免疫力。

sentences.en: Even if it turns out that vaccine protection wanes over time, we're still talking solid partial immunity.
sentences.zh: 即使疫苗保护力随时间减弱，我们谈论的仍然是稳固的部分免疫力。

sentences.en: That's not the case for people in poorer countries, huge numbers of people in poorer countries.
sentences.zh: 但贫困国家的人们并非如此，贫困国家有大量人口，

sentences.en: They don't have any protection against the virus at all.
sentences.zh: 他们对病毒没有任何保护。

sentences.en: And that's the priority if your goal is to prevent more deaths, more hospitalizations.
sentences.zh: 如果你的目标是防止更多的死亡和住院，那才是优先事项。

sentences.en: Well, Rebecca, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，丽贝卡，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Indonesia has become the newest epicenter of the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，印度尼西亚已成为疫情的最新震中，

sentences.en: surpassing India and Brazil to become the country with the world's highest count of new infections.
sentences.zh: 超过印度和巴西，成为全球新增感染人数最多的国家。

sentences.en: The surge there is part of a wave of outbreaks across Southeast Asia, where vaccination rates are low and countries had, until recently, kept the virus relatively well contained.
sentences.zh: 那里的激增是东南亚疫情浪潮的一部分，这些地区的疫苗接种率很低，且直到最近，各国对病毒的控制还相对较好。

sentences.en: Vietnam, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand are also facing their largest outbreaks yet.
sentences.zh: 越南、马来西亚、缅甸和泰国也正面临有史以来最大的疫情爆发。

sentences.en: And the death toll from historic flooding in Belgium and Germany has exceeded 180 people and is expected to keep growing as the waters recede and rescue operations intensify.
sentences.zh: 比利时和德国历史性洪灾造成的死亡人数已超过 180 人，随着水位下降和救援行动的加强，预计人数还会继续增加。

sentences.en: German meteorologists called it the worst flooding in at least 500 years.
sentences.zh: 德国气象学家称这是至少 500 年来最严重的洪水。

sentences.en: On Sunday, German Chancellor Angela Merkel met with survivors, telling them, that the German language has no words for the devastation.
sentences.zh: 周日，德国总理安格拉·默克尔会见了幸存者，告诉他们，德语中已经找不到词汇来形容这场灾难了。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Eric Krupke, Diana Nguyen, and Rob Zipko.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由埃里克·克鲁普克、戴安娜·阮和罗布·齐普科制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and Paige Cowett, contains original music from Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周和佩奇·考维特编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter 秀》，我们正准备迎接节假日的客人。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全遮光才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter 秀》。
